elysiumalmanac.claim.unknown: No such step in the book.

elysiumalmanac.quest.drawer: One thing, a lot of it
elysiumalmanac.quest.reward_waiting: Done — the reward is yours to take.
elysiumalmanac.task.web: Hold %s nodes on the Ledger Web
elysiumalmanac.why.a_door_of_stone: The game has eleven wooden doors and one of iron. This is a door of stone, and like the iron one it wants redstone rather than a hand.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_reason_to_choose: Reach, and nothing else at all. You will hit things before they hit you, and you will be very sorry the first time one gets inside it.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_road: Paving is worth most to whatever is slowest, which is the opposite of what you would guess and is the reason a cart on a road beats a hauler off one.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_wall_that_joins: Fences of stone, with a gate in them. They reach for each other and not for the oak fence next door, which is the whole difficulty with fences.
elysiumalmanac.why.a_window: Panes in anything at all, which the game does not have: it has glass and it has iron bars, and nothing between them in any material you like.
elysiumalmanac.why.accelerator: A room of pots works on torches. A room that keeps up with a factory needs a factory.
elysiumalmanac.why.alternator: Rotation in, power out, six times what a dynamo manages. It draws more torque than one water wheel can push.
elysiumalmanac.why.arc_furnace: 512 FE a tick, which is twice what a copper wire will carry. This is the machine that teaches you voltage.
elysiumalmanac.why.assembler: The core plans and builds nothing. Four assemblers is four jobs at once; sixteen is as many as one core will run, and every one of them is a machine on the grid.
elysiumalmanac.why.assembly_core: It reads every recipe the game has loaded, works out what a request would take, and tells you before it touches a single item in your drawers.
elysiumalmanac.why.brass_shaft: Timber shears above 64 rpm. Brass takes 192, and nothing in the second age will run on less.
elysiumalmanac.why.broad_tool: Clears a three-by-three, costs a point of durability for every block of it, and swings slower than the pickaxe it is standing in for. All three of those are on purpose.
elysiumalmanac.why.bronze: Three copper and a tin. The first alloy, and the first time the chain has a step in it.
elysiumalmanac.why.cart: It runs on anything that burns, carries nine stacks and loses to walking over rough ground — which is the whole reason you laid the road first.
elysiumalmanac.why.casing: A tier four machine runs on the top wire in the game. You have reached the end of the material chain.
elysiumalmanac.why.cell: Every grid until now spent what it made the tick it made it. A cell is the first time surplus is worth having.
elysiumalmanac.why.centrifuge: The hungriest machine in the age, and the only route to reactor fuel.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.ascent: Power you can keep, and the first thing that can kill you.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.automation: The warehouse stops being somewhere you look things up and starts being somewhere you ask for them.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.first_light: Rotation, and nothing that needs power at all.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.foundry: Alloys, and the top of the material chain.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.reconstructio: Steel, wire, and the first grid.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_dark: Something to hit things with, and the things.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_homestead: Somewhere worth coming back to, and what happens if you do not.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.the_wilds: Knowing where anything is, which is most of knowing what to do next.
elysiumalmanac.why.chapter.warehouse: Somewhere to put all of it.
elysiumalmanac.why.controller: Every drawer on its bus behaves as one inventory. Point a hopper at it and it finds the right drawer.
elysiumalmanac.why.coolant: Four channels. A bare core at full throttle settles at several times meltdown; three channels is not enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.copper_wire: A grid divides what it has: everything on it gets the same share. Copper carries 256 before it burns.
elysiumalmanac.why.crank: Every machine in the first age is turned by something. A crank is the something you can afford on day one.
elysiumalmanac.why.crusher: What the millstone becomes, at industrial scale and on a wire.
elysiumalmanac.why.drawer: A drawer holds one kind and thousands of it, costs nothing to run, and you can read how full it is across a room.
elysiumalmanac.why.enricher: The last rung of the ore ladder. Nothing above this does better.
elysiumalmanac.why.first_blade: Six shapes of weapon here, and this is the quick one. It does less per hit than almost anything else and gets more hits in than all of it.
elysiumalmanac.why.fuel: One piece runs a reactor at full throttle for five minutes. You will want a supply before you light one.
elysiumalmanac.why.hive: Two flowers a bee. Too few and it slows down rather than stopping, so go and plant something.
elysiumalmanac.why.invar: Two iron and a nickel. What a second-tier machine casing is.
elysiumalmanac.why.look_up: There are five worlds besides this one, and waygates that open at ruined-portal frequency. Go and find one.
elysiumalmanac.why.luna: No air, no weather, and a crop that grows in vacuum and nothing else.
elysiumalmanac.why.millstone: Cobblestone to gravel, bone to meal, ore to more ore later. The first machine that pays for itself.
elysiumalmanac.why.motor: Electricity back into rotation. Your first machine hall does not stop being useful — it stops being hand-cranked.
elysiumalmanac.why.plate: You will need a great deal of it. A factory is a thing you build with a factory.
elysiumalmanac.why.pot: One block, stackable in a room, feedable by a hopper. It wants light 9 or nothing grows.
elysiumalmanac.why.reactor: Prod it: it tells you the temperature now and the one this setting will reach. Do the arithmetic before you turn it up.
elysiumalmanac.why.road: A road is worth laying because of how much of a journey it saves, which means it is worth most to whatever is slowest. Build it before the vehicle, not after.
elysiumalmanac.why.rock: Everybody builds a cobblestone generator anyway. This one is a block, and it has tiers.
elysiumalmanac.why.rolling_mill: Plate is what every machine above this is skinned in. Nothing in the first age could make a sheet.
elysiumalmanac.why.saw: Six planks to a log instead of four, and the cheapest planks in the game from then on.
elysiumalmanac.why.seed: Slowly, on purpose: a farm is meant to lose to a mine until it is a deliberate industrial project.
elysiumalmanac.why.separator: Ore in, twice the metal out. The reason the second age exists.
elysiumalmanac.why.servo: It drives an Age I line at 1024 rpm, which no shaft below ascendant survives. Rebuild the old hall in something stronger.
elysiumalmanac.why.shaft: A shaft carries rotation. Prod any part of a line and it tells you what the whole line is doing.
elysiumalmanac.why.smelter: The only machine the fourth age adds. Everything else it needs, you already built.
elysiumalmanac.why.solar: Three FE a tick, which is almost nothing. A panel is not a generator — it is the reason a cell is worth building.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_else: Bind one, and then bind another, and the distance between them costs power rather than time. The price rises with distance and stops rising.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_to_put_thin: The other half of what a room needs. Every shape here can be broken back down, and none of them gives back more than it cost.
elysiumalmanac.why.somewhere_to_sit: Twelve shapes, sixteen materials, and not one of them needs a texture the game did not already have. Start with somewhere to sit down.
elysiumalmanac.why.spallet: A spallet is the smallest thing that hunts you and the one you will meet first. It comes apart when you hit it and the pieces keep coming.
elysiumalmanac.why.stainless: Three steel and a nickel. An alloy of an alloy, which is where a furnace stops being enough.
elysiumalmanac.why.starsteel: An alloy of an alloy of an alloy, and the only thing a tier four casing can be made of. Nothing in the pack is above it, so a starsteel machine is the last one you build.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel: The first thing the age makes for itself, and the gate to the top tier of wire, the diesel engine and the separator.
elysiumalmanac.why.steel_drawer: Four kinds and eight thousand of each. This is what a factory's wall is made of.
elysiumalmanac.why.terminal: No screen and nothing to search: right-click it holding a thing for a stack of that thing, crouch for one. What comes back is how many steps and how many machine-runs, or why not.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_compass: Pick somewhere and it points at the nearest one. It looks the same distance for everything, however rare, which is why it does not make the server stutter.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_crate: Use it on a villager to pick them up and on a block to put them down. Their trades, their level and their restock clock all come with them.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_grave: Everything you were carrying goes into a grave where you fell, sized to what you actually had, and nobody else can open it until you have plainly given up on it.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_heavy_answer: The hardest single hit in the pack and the slowest swing behind it. Bring it to something large and leave it at home the rest of the time.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_hollow_lord: It waited a long time for something, and it was not you. Bring the heaviest thing you have and do it in daylight if you can arrange that.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_long_answer: Slow, enormous, and it takes two more things with it on every swing. The answer to being surrounded, and a poor answer to anything else.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_narrow_answer: Half of what it does goes through armour rather than into it. Against anything in plate it is the best thing here; against anything else it is not.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_siege_beast: Three metres of it, and it goes through the wall rather than round it. The hardest thing in the bestiary and the best-paid.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_stalker: You will hear it stop following you, and that is the bad part. The top of the prowlers, and the fastest thing that will ever chase you.
elysiumalmanac.why.the_three_families: A drayhulk will not be knocked back and a carrier burns at dawn. Everything in the dark is one of three families and each wants a different answer.
elysiumalmanac.why.transformer: The one block allowed two voltages on it. Everywhere else, the higher one destroys the lower.
elysiumalmanac.why.transmuter: Dissolve something and you get most of its worth back as motes; spend motes and you get back anything you have dissolved before. A round trip always loses a tenth, so there is no loop in it worth riding.
elysiumalmanac.why.turbine: A firebox and a boiler. It only burns when something on the grid actually wants the power.
elysiumalmanac.why.water_wheel: A crank stops when you walk away. A water wheel does not, and that is the whole of the first age's lesson.
elysiumalmanac.why.waystone: Bind two and you can jump between them for a price the grid pays. An unwired stone fills from nothing, so the short way home costs a minute; wire it and the minute goes away.
elysiumalmanac.why.welcome: Everything in this pack hangs off four ages of machinery. You are at the bottom of the first one, and it needs no power.
elysiumalmanac.why.worth_the_trouble: The second rung of all three ladders. Every one of them is worth more than the thing below it, and that is a promise this pack actually checks.
